papers.title: Characterizing transition state in mouse vigilance with electroencephalogram-electromyogram hypnodensity.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This study characterized vigilance-state transitions in mice using EEG/EMG and expert annotations, finding distinct temporal dynamics across transition types, with NREMS-to-REMS transitions longest. An SVM classifier trained on stable-state features successfully predicted transition midpoints, providing a reproducible framework for quantifying sleep-wake transitions.

papers.title: REM Sleep Disengagement of β Oscillations Permits Rapid Dream Movements in Parkinsonism
papers.summary: In non-human primates with MPTP-induced parkinsonism, pathological beta oscillations and motor impairments were attenuated during REM sleep, with beta suppression preceding REM onset. This indicates that Parkinsonian network dysfunction is dynamically gated by brain state, and REM sleep disengages beta oscillations to permit rapid movements.

papers.title: ICA-S3M: switching state-space model guided automatic EEG artifact removal from independent components.
papers.summary: ICA-S3M is a two-stage pipeline for EEG artifact removal that combines ICA with a switching state-space model to separate neural oscillations from broadband EMG artifact. In simulations, it reduced RRMSE from 0.83 to 0.23 and improved SNR by 12.4 dB, outperforming a CNN and avoiding the CNN's 'alpha hallucination' failure.

papers.title: Diurnal time and sleep pressure modulate cerebrospinal fluid low-frequency oscillations in synchrony with wake-promoting nuclei
papers.summary: In a 34-hour sleep deprivation study, CSF low-frequency oscillations (LFOs) increased with time awake and showed diurnal fluctuation, peaking in early morning. CSF LFOs were associated with vigilance and reticular activating system activity, but not plasma norepinephrine, indicating independent modulation by time awake and diurnal time.

papers.title: PVT inhibition mitigates neuropathology and cognitive deficits in chronic cerebral hypoperfusion.
papers.summary: In a mouse model of chronic cerebral hypoperfusion, whole-brain mapping identified the paraventricular thalamus (PVT) as a persistently hyperactive hub. Chemogenetic inhibition of PVT early after ischemia reduced neuronal damage, improved cognitive performance, and enhanced sleep continuity, suggesting PVT as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Rapid associative spine enlargement is required for cognitive function and stable wakefulness
papers.summary: The authors developed SynC, a chemogenetic tool that selectively blocks rapid associative spine enlargement in mouse neocortical neurons. Acute inhibition of spine enlargement impaired cognitive behaviors and reduced pairwise spike correlations during wakefulness, while sparing baseline firing and gamma activity, indicating that rapid spine enlargement is required for stable awake cognition.

papers.title: Meta-Analysis of Face-Validity Indicators in Automatically Detected Dog Sleep Spindles.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis assessed face validity of automatically detected dog sleep spindles against three criteria from human EEG: event shortness, midline distribution of fast spindles, and amplitude-chirp association. All criteria were met in the majority of datasets, supporting the quality of the automatic detection method and the dog as a model for sleep spindle research.

papers.title: Aftereffects of 1-week chronic intermittent hypoxia on the jaw muscle electromyographic activities during sleep in young adult rats.
papers.summary: The study investigated effects of one-week chronic intermittent hypoxia (CIH) on jaw muscle activity during sleep in young adult rats. CIH increased FosB expression in trigeminal premotor regions and noradrenergic innervation of the trigeminal motor nucleus, and selectively enhanced digastric muscle activity on arousal from sleep without altering overall sleep architecture.

papers.title: Automated autism spectrum disorder detection using EEG signals and time-frequency visibility graphs.
papers.summary: The authors proposed a dual-domain EEG-based ASD classification framework combining time-frequency transforms (STFT, DWT, WVD, SLT) with Horizontal Visibility Graph network features and machine learning classifiers. The DWT-HVG approach with a soft voting ensemble achieved 93.54% accuracy and 98.17% AUC, outperforming other transforms.

papers.title: White matter hyperintensity drives EEG microstate abnormalities in arteriosclerotic cerebral small vessel disease.
papers.summary: This study analyzed EEG microstates in patients with white matter hyperintensity (WMH) with and without dementia and healthy controls. WMH patients showed reduced temporal parameters of microstate C and altered transitions, correlated with WMH volume and cognitive scores; SVM and logistic regression models distinguished groups with up to 79% accuracy.

papers.title: An EEG-based fatigue detection framework integrating interpretable feature selection and efficient temporal modeling.
papers.summary: The paper introduces AXELLSTM, an EEG-based cross-subject fatigue detection framework combining interpretable feature selection (ANOVA, XGBoost, L1-regularized sparse selection) with an EfficientLSTM model incorporating attention mechanisms. It achieved a Macro-F1 of 0.7143 ± 0.2452 under leave-one-subject-out validation, with 18 stable EEG channels identified across frontal, parietal, and occipital regions, demonstrating a favorable balance between accuracy and model complexity.

papers.title: Single-channel gamma burst dynamics and adaptive deep learning for robust EEG motor state decoding.
papers.summary: The paper introduces a compact decoding framework that models gamma burst dynamics via analytic wavelet transform and combines them with spectral features using a multi-stream adaptive deep learning model. It achieves competitive performance in single-channel EEG motor decoding and improves cross-session accuracy by more than 10% over non-adaptive baselines on the WAY-EEG-GAL dataset.

papers.title: Respiratory phase shapes brain-heart dynamics: evidence from recurrence analysis of EEG band power and heart rate.
papers.summary: The study investigated respiratory-phase-dependent modulation of brain-heart interactions during controlled breathing in 15 healthy subjects, using EEG band power and heart rate with recurrence quantification analysis. It found that inhale-hold was associated with increased gamma power, higher recurrence, and elevated heart rate, while exhale-hold showed decreases, indicating distinct autonomic and dynamical states.

papers.title: DTI-ALPS as a marker of glymphatic function: Review of the literature findings, methodology, and interpretation.
papers.summary: This review summarizes the DTI-ALPS technique as a non-invasive MRI marker of glymphatic system function, covering its methodology, applications, and critique. It reports exponential growth in publications, frequent use in neurodegenerative diseases, and concludes that DTI-ALPS is sensitive but non-specific for white matter damage and neuroinflammation.

papers.title: Environmental context outweighs early methamphetamine exposure in shaping behavioral and glutamatergic outcomes in rats.
papers.summary: The study examined interactions between early methamphetamine exposure and environmental conditions on behavior and glutamate levels in adolescent rats. It found that environmental factors (enrichment and housing) had stronger effects on behavior and region-specific glutamate levels than early MA exposure, with task-dependent outcomes.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Functional Connectivity and Independent Correlates of Cognitive Impairment in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation.
papers.summary: This study investigated resting-state EEG functional connectivity in atrial fibrillation patients with and without cognitive impairment, finding reduced alpha-band connectivity independently associated with cognitive impairment and a good discriminatory ability for a model combining clinical variables and alpha-band wPLI.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture improves neurocognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation: an experimental study based on hippocampal neurogenesis and synaptic plasticity.
papers.summary: This experimental study in rats showed that electroacupuncture at cervical acupoints improved cognitive impairment induced by chronic sleep deprivation, likely by promoting hippocampal neurogenesis and restoring synaptic plasticity in the dentate gyrus.

papers.title: Associations of Plasma Total Tau Level and MMSE Score With Polysomnographic Data in Middle-Aged Men With Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: This pilot study in middle-aged men with severe obstructive sleep apnea found that plasma total tau levels were positively correlated with apnea-hypopnea index and negatively with deep sleep duration and oxygen saturation, while MMSE scores negatively correlated with apnea-hypopnea index, oxygen desaturation index, and arousal index.

papers.title: Armillariella tabescens polysaccharide targets microglial glycolysis to alleviate sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation through the mTOR signaling pathway.
papers.journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
papers.summary: This study isolated a polysaccharide from Armillariella tabescens and showed it alleviates sleep deprivation-induced neuroinflammation and cognitive deficits by inhibiting mTOR signaling, correcting glycolytic reprogramming, and promoting microglial M2 polarization.

papers.title: Negative BOLD response to interictal discharges in epilepsy using intracranial EEG-fMRI.
authors: the, Calgary Comprehensive Epilepsy Program collaborators
papers.summary: This intracranial EEG-fMRI study in patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy found that positive BOLD responses to interictal discharges were closer to epileptogenic tissue than negative BOLD responses, while negative BOLD responses overlapped more with the default mode network, suggesting they reflect network deactivation.

papers.title: Longitudinal associations between sleepiness and sleep disturbances across pregnancy.
papers.journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal study of 3808 pregnant women found that sleepiness followed a U-shaped trajectory across pregnancy, while insomnia increased from 19.1% to 59.1%. Sleepiness was consistently associated with insomnia, short sleep duration, sleep loss, and snoring from midpregnancy onwards, suggesting screening for underlying sleep disturbances in pregnant women reporting sleepiness.

papers.title: Chronotype, temporal eating patterns, and sleep behaviors among physically active university students: A cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 200 physically active university students found that later first and last caloric intake were independently associated with lower Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire scores (β = -0.435 and -0.422, respectively), explaining 51.1% of the variance. Evening-type participants had poorer sleep behaviors and later caloric intake compared to morning-types.

papers.title: Chronic corticosterone exposure disrupts bile acids homeostasis associated with circadian dysfunction in the liver of chickens.
papers.summary: This study in broiler chickens found that chronic corticosterone exposure disrupted the hepatic circadian clock, reducing BMAL1 and REV-ERBβ mesors and suppressing REV-ERBβ amplitude. Corticosterone increased CYP8B1 mesor and amplitude, advanced acrophases of FXR and SHP, and altered bile acid levels, while dexamethasone upregulated MRP2 expression and promoted its membrane translocation, enhancing apical bile acid efflux.

papers.title: Nocturnal heart rate variability in Parkinson's disease: associations with autonomic dysfunction, cognitive function, and mood symptoms.
papers.summary: This study analyzed nocturnal heart rate variability (HRV) from polysomnography in 36 Parkinson's disease (PD) patients and 20 healthy controls. PD patients showed lower low-frequency power (LF) and LF/HF ratio, and higher high-frequency power (HF) during NREM and REM sleep, indicating reduced sympathetic influence. In PD, better executive function and processing speed correlated with higher HF and lower LF/HF during NREM, while subjective autonomic symptoms correlated with poorer cognition and mood.

papers.title: CEREBROVASCULAR EVENTS AND NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS WITH ALTERATIONS IN POLYSOMNOGRAPHIC INDICATORS FOLLOWING CARDIAC SURGERY.
papers.summary: Prospective study of 104 cardiac surgery patients examined postoperative neurocognitive and cerebrovascular complications with polysomnography; PSG alterations correlated with cognitive impairment, and Citicoline improved MoCA scores and sleep parameter stabilization by day 30 (p=0.0016).

papers.title: Association between habitual sleep duration and Alzheimer's disease: A cross-sectional study based on NHANES 2007-2018.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 29,692 NHANES participants found a significant positive association between longer sleep duration and Alzheimer's disease prevalence, suggesting sleep time as a predictive tool for AD risk assessment.

papers.title: Adolescent depression recognition and symptom prediction based on multi-view EEG network: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: This exploratory study developed a Multi-view Adaptive Graph Convolutional Network (MVA-GCN) based on resting-state EEG to recognize adolescent depression. The MVA-GCN achieved 99.84% accuracy in classifying 44 MDD and 30 healthy controls, compared to 86.43% for questionnaire-based models. Occipital and fronto-central regions contributed most, and increased gamma-band functional connectivity and reduced alpha-band power were potential correlates, but findings need replication in larger cohorts.

papers.title: From bench to bedside: current evidence and prospects for acupuncture in managing perioperative neurocognitive disorders.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on acupuncture for perioperative neurocognitive disorders, proposing a multi-target neuroprotective mechanism centered on the gut-brain axis that regulates microbiota, neural circuits, and inflammatory pathways; clinical value is supported by current evidence.

papers.title: Adverse experiences in childhood and adolescence in relation to sleep health in adulthood: An overview of systematic reviews and a global evidence map.
authors: World Sleep Society Global Adolescent Sleep Project Taskforce
papers.summary: Overview of 12 systematic reviews found consistent associations between childhood/adolescent adversity and poorer adult sleep health, but evidence certainty was low; research is concentrated in the Americas and Europe with no low-income country representation.

papers.title: AI-assisted identification and in vitro validation of a MyD88 pathway modulator for inflammatory airway signalling.
papers.summary: Study combined AI-based de novo ligand design with in vitro assays to identify a MyD88 pathway modulator that reduced TLR4/MyD88/NF-κB signaling and pro-inflammatory cytokines in airway cells, showing potential for inflammatory airway disease therapy.

papers.title: Cross-Sectional Associations of Insomnia, Social Dysfunction, Suicidality, and Depressive Symptoms in Rural Adults with Schizophrenia: A Sex-Stratified Analysis.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 931 rural adults with schizophrenia in China found that insomnia, suicidality, and social dysfunction were associated with depressive symptoms, with no sex differences in these associations. Females had higher scores on all symptom measures, and insomnia showed direct and indirect associations with depression via social dysfunction and suicidality.

papers.title: Cardiac Autonomic Modulation in Seizure Disorders With and Without Interictal Epileptiform Discharges: A Retrospective Heart Rate Variability Analysis Using Archived Digital EEG Recordings.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared heart rate variability (HRV) parameters among seizure disorder patients with and without interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs) and a non-seizure comparison group using ECG from archived EEG recordings. Patients with seizure disorders showed lower vagally mediated HRV (pNN50, total power, HF power) than the comparison group, but no significant HRV differences were found between the two seizure groups, indicating IEDs were not associated with additional autonomic alterations.

papers.title: Association Between Nocturnal Oxygen Desaturation and the Severity of Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Study.
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 55 OSA patients found that the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) was positively correlated with oxygen desaturation index and T90, and negatively correlated with minimum and mean nocturnal SpO2. The associations were statistically significant, supporting a relationship between OSA severity and nocturnal hypoxemia.

papers.title: Parent and child-reported acceptability and preference of pediatric home sleep apnea testing versus In-lab polysomnography: a pilot study.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: This pilot study of 15 children comparing home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) with in-lab polysomnography (PSG) found that HSAT was feasible and acceptable to most parents and children, with 60% of parents and 33% of children preferring HSAT. However, parents frequently had to adjust sensors (especially nasal cannula and pulse oximeter), suggesting improvements in sensor stability could enhance acceptability.

papers.title: Digital screen exposure and migraine burden: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 studies with 14,763 participants found that higher digital screen exposure was associated with 60% greater odds of migraine/headache (pooled OR 1.60, 95% CI 1.38-1.86), though certainty was low. Proposed mechanisms included blue light-mediated retinal ganglion cell activation, melatonin suppression, and trigeminovascular hyperexcitability.

papers.title: Associations of sleep duration variability and depressive symptoms with gastrointestinal disease among middle-aged and older adults: A cohort study.
papers.summary: This cohort study using CHARLS and HRS data found that greater sleep duration variability was associated with an increased risk of gastrointestinal disease, with the highest quartile showing odds ratios of 1.43 and 1.84 in the two cohorts. Depressive symptoms partially mediated this association, suggesting that both sleep variability and mental health may contribute to gastrointestinal disease risk.

papers.title: Association between the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index and obstructive sleep apnea risk: Mediating role of body mass index in U.S. adults.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional analysis of 4,564 U.S. adults found that each unit increase in the C-reactive protein-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI) was associated with 43% higher odds of obstructive sleep apnea, with BMI mediating 56.3% of the association. CTI showed slightly better discrimination than traditional markers but modest overall performance.

papers.title: Teaching-research conflict and self-reported strain in early academic careers: Selective role investment among postdoctoral teacher-researchers.
papers.summary: This qualitative study of 30 postdoctoral researchers in Chinese higher education found that participants responded to teaching-research conflict through selective role investment, such as protecting writing time and compressing teaching preparation, which was perceived as necessary for career viability but sometimes caused strain. Findings conceptualize career adaptation as a patterned redistribution of time under unequal career consequences.

papers.title: Single-Site ALK-Positive Histiocytosis With TFG-ALK Fusion: Expanding the Clinical Spectrum of This Rare Entity.
papers.journal: The American journal of case reports
papers.summary: This case report describes the first instance of single-site ALK-positive histiocytosis with a TFG-ALK fusion in a 1.6-cm pulmonary nodule, treated with surgical resection alone and remaining disease-free. The finding expands the clinical spectrum, suggesting this fusion can be associated with localized disease and an indolent course.

papers.title: (Cost-)effectiveness of a combined lifestyle intervention integrated into standard care for low back pain compared to usual care for people with persistent non-specific low back pain who are overweight or obese: Protocol for a randomised controlled trial with parallel economic and process evaluations (Back2Health).
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomized controlled trial (Back2Health) evaluating the (cost-)effectiveness of a combined lifestyle intervention integrated into standard care versus usual care for 318 adults with persistent non-specific low back pain and overweight/obesity. Co-primary outcomes are physical functioning and physical activity over 36 months.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
